USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Proceed with the Section 301 tariff action against China, but keep its scope calibrated and explicitly leave the door open to negotiation, so we press our leverage without triggering a self-defeating tariff war. Continue the Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs and solar/washer actions as applied, but signal willingness to engage China and our allies on a rules-based path to avoid a broad unilateral action that alienates the EU/Japan and hands China legal cover to retaliate. The objective is to convert our strong-negotiating position into real concessions on IP and forced technology transfer, not to maximize the tariff bill.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat reading is favorable-to-neutral for the US because we are the initiating party holding the initiative, and the US economy shows no trade-war drag: consumer sentiment is elevated (101.4 in March), industrial production is still climbing (102.2), and the dollar is broadly stable — there is no material recession risk from the dispute yet. The Section 301 investigation has run since August 2017 with clear bipartisan support (timeline Aug 14, 2017; Politico Mar 7, 2018 reports the tariff action is 'nearly ready to go'). Against that, the risks that keep this from being a clean −0.5 opportunity are the substantial downsides of overreach: legal analyses (Cato/Newsweek, Jan 5, 2018) warn broad unilateral Section 301 tariffs are likely WTO-inconsistent and would be condemned by other members, and Section 232 has already drawn ally backlash, with Mattis and McMaster warning the global tariffs could damage key allies (NatLawReview, Mar 5, 2018). Those self-inflicted risks — WTO challenge, ally friction, and likely Chinese retaliation against US farm and export goods — argue for escalating the tariffs we are committed to but keeping scope disciplined and preserving a negotiation lane. Hence threat_score −0.35 (mild opportunity, not existential) and action_score −0.45 (moderate escalation: raise/expand tariffs via the Section 301 action while signaling readiness to talk).
key_factors: US holds the initiative: Section 301 investigation since Aug 2017; solar/washer Section 201 (Jan 2018) and steel/aluminum Section 232 (Mar 1/8, 2018) tariffs already imposed
US economy shows no trade-war drag: sentiment 101.4, industrial production 102.2 rising, dollar broadly stable, no material recession risk
Mildly favorable leverage: bipartisan support for 301 (Politico Mar 7), opportunity to extract IP/tech-transfer concessions and onshore industry

Overreach risk: broad unilateral Section 301 tariffs likely WTO-inconsistent and would be condemned (Cato/Jan 5), ally alienation from Section 232 (Mattis/McMaster opposition, Mar 5), and likely Chinese retaliation against US exports
Recommend calibrated moderate escalation preserving a negotiation lane
action_score and action_level: moderate escalation consistent with escalate_tariffs band
threat_score and score both set to −0.35
